name: Insider Trading and Market Abuse Detection
title: Insider Trading and Market Abuse Detection
answer: Insider trading and market abuse detection covers the surveillance of trading activity and related communications for conduct such as insider dealing, market manipulation, spoofing, layering, wash trading, and improper disclosure. It applies across equities, fixed income, derivatives, commodities, and crypto assets, and across venues including exchanges, dark pools, and over-the-counter markets. The work sits with compliance, legal, and surveillance teams at banks, brokers, asset managers, and exchanges, and with regulators who supervise them. The aim is to surface patterns and relationships that are hard to see in manual review, then route them to human investigators for judgment.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Insider trading and market abuse detection covers the surveillance of trading activity and related communications for conduct such as insider dealing, market manipulation, spoofing, layering, wash trading, and improper disclosure. It applies across equities, fixed income, derivatives, commodities, and crypto assets, and across venues including exchanges, dark pools, and over-the-counter markets. The work sits with compliance, legal, and surveillance teams at banks, brokers, asset managers, and exchanges, and with regulators who supervise them. The aim is to surface patterns and relationships that are hard to see in manual review, then route them to human investigators for judgment.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Detection systems run on a mix of market data feeds, order and trade records, reference data, corporate actions, news, and employee communications such as email, chat, and voice. These inputs land in streaming platforms, time-series databases, graph stores, and data lakes, often in the cloud but sometimes on premises for latency or confidentiality reasons. Natural language processing pipelines handle text and speech, while rule engines and machine learning models score activity in near real time or in batch. The infrastructure must preserve data lineage, access controls, and retention schedules so that any alert can be reconstructed later.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work combines rules that encode known abuse patterns with statistical and machine learning models that flag deviations from normal behavior. Analysts use anomaly detection, clustering, sequence models, and network analysis to connect traders, accounts, instruments, and communications. Alerts are triaged in case management systems, where investigators gather evidence, interview staff, and decide whether to escalate or close. Models are tuned and backtested against historical cases, and explainability tools help reviewers understand why a particular trade or message was flagged.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk turn on privacy and employment law, cross-border data transfer rules, legal privilege, and recordkeeping obligations. Surveillance programs must document data provenance, model validation, access controls, and audit trails, and they must avoid unfair or discriminatory outcomes. False positives can harm employees and waste resources, while false negatives can leave misconduct undetected. Regulators expect firms to have credible surveillance, clear escalation paths, and evidence that models are monitored and governed over time.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The field is moving toward more use of unstructured data, including chat, voice, and video, and toward generative tools that summarize evidence and draft investigation notes. Surveillance is expanding across asset classes and venues, including crypto and decentralized finance, where transparency and identity are uneven. Regulators are also building their own analytics capacity, which increases expectations for firms' detection and reporting. Human judgment remains central, because context, intent, and materiality are not fully captured by any model.
